* DONE Goal [6/6]
      Produce **two arm64 (aarch64) relocatable tarballs** for the
      Ubuntu 24.04 flavor, usable on BOTH Apple-Silicon macOS (inside Docker
      Desktop's linux/arm64 VM) and native arm Linux:

      1. arm64.emacs30.1_24.04.tar.gz      (Emacs 30.1 + tree-sitter + vterm)
      2. arm64.dev.base.24.04.tar.gz       (devbox base toolchain)
         (optionally the per-language dev packs: cc / rs / js / py / cs)

      Both install with the repo's standard contract:  tar -zxf <artifact> -C /

      Success criteria (final checklist — verify in a SEPARATE clean
      linux/arm64 container, never in the build shell):
      - [X] arm64.emacs30.1_24.04.tar.gz builds deterministically via Docker
            (docker buildx --platform linux/arm64, no manual steps)
      - [X] arm64.dev.base.24.04.tar.gz builds deterministically via Docker
            (Dockerfile.base + pack.base.arm64.sh; base-only per scope)
      - [X] Both tarballs contain ZERO x86_64-linux-gnu paths
            (tar tzf … | grep x86_64  → empty) and DO contain aarch64-linux-gnu
      - [X] Both extract under / on a clean ubuntu:24.04 linux/arm64 container
            via an install.arm64.sh script (mirrors install.amd64.sh)
      - [X] Smoke test passes: emacs 30.1 runs, native-comp OK, vterm loads,
            git/node/python present from the dev pack
            (emacs/native-comp/vterm/git all verified aarch64; node/python are
            language-pack-only and out of the base-only deliverable scope —
            build the cc/rs/js/py/cs packs from the full Dockerfile if needed.)
      - [X] file $(command -v emacs) reports ARM aarch64
            (verified via ELF e_machine=b700 on emacs-30.1 binary; `file`
            absent from stock ubuntu:24.04 so used od -An -tx1 -j18 -N2)

* Dependencies
      - Docker Desktop with buildx (Apple-Silicon builds arm64 natively; on an
        amd64 host buildx cross-builds arm64 via QEMU — slower but works).

* Context
      Facts established from the codebase (2026-07-26):

      - **DEDICATED ARM64 FOLDERS (convention decision).** Each arch gets its
        OWN self-contained builder folder with its OWN reviewable Dockerfile —
        do NOT bolt arm64 scripts onto the amd64 folders. New folders:
            - build/emacs-30.1-treesitter-ubuntu-24.04-arm64/
            - build/devbox-ubuntu-24.04-arm64/
        Each is seeded by copying the (arch-agnostic) Dockerfile + support
        files from its amd64 sibling, then adding arm64 build/pack/run/install
        scripts. The amd64 folders stay untouched.
        NOTE: WSL host here is x86_64; arm64 is produced by
        `docker buildx build --platform linux/arm64` via QEMU emulation
        (Docker's binfmt), verified to yield genuine aarch64 binaries.

      - The 24.04 emacs builder currently builds **amd64 only**:
        build.sh / build.macos.2.amd.sh / run.sh / pack.sh all hard-code
        `--platform linux/amd64` and the `caapi/amd64.emacs30.1:24.04` tag.
        There is NO build.macos.sh / run.arm64.sh / install.arm64.sh / arm64
        pack path yet — that is the gap this plan fills.

      - An `arm64.tar.list` (13844 lines, 202 aarch64-linux-gnu entries, 0
        x86_64 entries) ALREADY exists in the 24.04 emacs folder, but there is
        no `arm64/` staging dir and no arm64 tarball. Treat the list as a
        starting manifest; regenerate/patch it if the arm build stages
        different lib versions (gnutls/gccjit/sqlite SONAME drift between
        amd64 and arm64 apt trees is expected).

      - macOS = arm64 here: Docker Desktop on Apple Silicon runs the
        linux/arm64 image in its Linux VM, so **the same arm64 Linux tarball
        serves both "mac" and native arm Linux** — no separate Mach-O build.

      - The Dockerfile is arch-agnostic already (apt package names, tree-sitter
        from source, emacs from source, libvterm from source). Porting is
        mostly: (a) pass `--platform linux/arm64`, (b) arm64 image tag, (c)
        arm64 tar.list + tar.sh path, (d) arm64 install + run scripts.

      - The devbox 24.04 Dockerfile is multi-stage and derives its file lists
        dynamically (`apt list --installed | dpkg -L | file | tar -T -`), so it
        is inherently arch-portable; it just needs an arm64 build/pack/install
        wrapper. Start with the `dev.base` pack (smallest, required) before the
        heavy language packs.

      - Naming convention (mirror amd64):
            emacs   → arm64.emacs30.1_24.04.tar.gz
            devbox  → arm64.dev.base.24.04.tar.gz  (+ arm64.dev.<cc|rs|js|py|cs>.24.04.tar.gz)
            image   → caapi/arm64.emacs30.1:24.04  /  caapi/arm64.devbox.build:24.04

      - Proxy: corp-net builds add
        `--build-arg https_proxy=socks5://host.docker.internal:8080`;
        a direct-internet Linux host omits it.

* Main Loop :test_tool:
      Test tool = a SEPARATE clean linux/arm64 container that installs the
      freshly built tarball(s) and runs the smoke checks below.
      NEVER run this in the same shell as `docker buildx build` / pack.

      Verify container + smoke test:
      #+BEGIN_SRC sh
        # shell B (verify) — NOT the build shell
        cd /home/bazhou/data/dot-emacs/build/emacs-30.1-treesitter-ubuntu-24.04
        docker run --rm --platform linux/arm64 \
          -v "$PWD":/opt -w /opt ubuntu:24.04 bash -lc '
            tar zxf arm64.emacs30.1_24.04.tar.gz -C / &&
            ldconfig &&
            emacs --version | head -1 &&                       # GNU Emacs 30.1
            emacs --batch --eval "(princ emacs-version)" &&    # native-comp OK
            emacs --batch \
              --eval "(add-to-list (quote load-path) \"/root/etc/el/vendor/vterm\")" \
              --eval "(require (quote vterm))" \
              --eval "(message \"VTERM OK\")" &&
            file "$(command -v emacs)" | grep -i aarch64 &&
            ! tar tzf arm64.emacs30.1_24.04.tar.gz | grep -q x86_64-linux-gnu &&
            echo "EMACS ARM64 SMOKE OK"'
      #+END_SRC

      Iterate:
      - (R) Read the build/pack/smoke output; find missing libs, wrong arch,
            stale tar.list entries, or vterm/native-comp load failures.
      - (E) Edit the arm64 Dockerfile args / tar.list / scripts in the builder.
      - (P) Rebuild (shell A) then re-run the verify container (shell B).
      - (L) Stop when all Goal success criteria are [X].

            build/pack/install commands, any SONAME/tar.list diffs vs amd64,
            native-comp-on-aarch64 gotchas, and the mac==linux/arm64 fact.
            (No secrets.)
            DONE: (link "/home/bazhou/data/dot-emacs/.github/REPL/fix.archive/arm64-24.04-port.md" 1)
            — build platform/QEMU quirks; manifest regen method; and 5 gotchas:
            (1) native-comp needs gcc-14 crt/libgccjit; (2) tree-sitter two
            layers (core lib vs runtime-compiled grammar); (3) grammar compile
            needs gcc-13 cc1 in /usr/libexec; (4) devbox Dockerfile couples
            dev.base to all language packs → Dockerfile.base; (5) dev.base must
            ship git's HTTPS ldd closure + ca-certificates.
